title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a handwritten sheet written over the back of the typescript of 'Le groupe de Brauer III', §8; the faint underlying text continues the neighbouring pages. The ink notes belong to the cote-16 project: an abstract, algebraic formalism for Lefschetz operators inside a graded algebra C = ⊕ C^i of 'correspondences', meant as an axiomatisation of the standard conjectures (Poincaré-Hodge algebras).

(1) Setting. There is a dimension n. C^{2n} and C^{-2n} are the extreme graded pieces; morally Hom(H^0, H^{2n}) and Hom(H^{2n}, H^0), which have rank one. A 'Lefschetzian' element L of degree 2 comes with an inverse Lefschetz operator Λ of degree -2, as in an sl_2-pair (L, Λ). π_0 is the projector onto degree 0.

Start from a reference Lefschetz pair (L_0, Λ_0) for which L_0^n is 'admissible' ('bien'), i.e. a generator of C^{2n}. The identity L_0^n = L_0^n π_0 = L_0^n Λ^n L_0^n expresses that Λ^n L^n is the identity on degree 0.

Now take another Lefschetz pair (L, Λ̂). Write L^n = α L_0^n and Λ̂^n = β Λ_0^n, with α, β scalars, since the extreme pieces have rank one. Substituting gives L_0^n = αβ L_0^n π_0 = αβ L_0^n. As L_0^n is a basis, αβ = 1, so α and β are units. Conclusion: for any Lefschetzian L, L^n is a basis of C^{2n} and Λ̂^n is a basis of C^{-2n}.

(2) Open questions, partly illegible. There is a '?': whether a certain algebra ℰ is projective of finite type over the base ring. A model ℰ = 𝓛(M*) is considered, with M* graded (perhaps End of a graded module), 'degrés ≤ 4'. Then come remarks about elements of degree 2, 'pour la dim 6', and Lefschetz.

(3) Counterexample to the converse of (1). Take the commutative graded algebra generated by L, L' in degree 2 with relations L^4 = 0, L'^2 = LL', L^2 L' = L^3, L^3 L' = 0.
- Basis: 1 (deg 0); L, L' (deg 2); L^2, LL' (deg 4); L^3 (deg 6).
- Multiplication by L from deg 2 to deg 4 is an isomorphism, and L^3 ≠ 0, so L is Lefschetzian.
- Multiplication by L' sends both L and L' to LL', so it is not an isomorphism from H^2 to H^4: L' is not Lefschetzian.
- Yet L'^3 = L·L'^2 = L^2 L' = L^3, which generates the top degree.

So 'L^n is a generator of C^{2n}' does not imply 'L is Lefschetzian'. Purpose: pin down which conditions characterise Lefschetz elements in the abstract Poincaré-Hodge formalism.
errors: The toy algebra is not a Poincaré-duality algebra. The pairing H^2 × H^4 → H^6 has Gram matrix [[1,1],[1,1]] in the bases (L, L') and (L^2, LL'). So L − L' is killed by all of degree 4, and the example does not live in the intended category of 'Poincaré-Hodge' algebras. The conclusion (L'^3 = generator but L' not Lefschetz) is still true in genuine Poincaré-duality examples, e.g. suitable classes on (P^1)^3, so this is a flaw of the example rather than of the claim.

Notation in the αβ computation is inconsistent (Λ vs Λ̂ vs Λ̄, where α and β are placed). The argument is sound only if the base ring is such that x = αβx with x a basis forces αβ = 1, which is automatic since x is a basis of a free rank-one module.

ideas.what: Abstract Lefschetz element / sl_2-pair (L, Λ) in a graded algebra of correspondences, and the fact that L^n and Λ^n are bases of the rank-one extreme pieces C^{±2n}
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz operators in Kleiman's formalism of the standard conjectures; uniqueness of Λ given L
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Standard conjectures, 1969 Bombay); Kleiman (Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures, 1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), in general form; this specific lemma is unsure

ideas.what: Example of a degree-2 element L' with L'^n a top-degree generator but failing hard Lefschetz, in an algebra with two degree-2 generators
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the strong Lefschetz property despite nonzero top power; Lefschetz properties of Artinian algebras

ideas.what: Question whether the algebra ℰ (correspondences / End of a graded module) is projective of finite type over the coefficient ring
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness / projectivity of algebras of motivic correspondences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, motives; Jannsen 1992 (semisimplicity of numerical motives)

missed.claim: Grothendieck already treats the Lefschetz condition as a property of elements of an abstract finite-dimensional graded commutative algebra and tests it on small Artinian examples. This anticipates the later commutative-algebra study of weak/strong Lefschetz properties. However, his example lacks Poincaré duality and the observation itself is elementary.
missed.quote: L est Lefschetzien, L' ne l'est pas, bien que L'^3=L^3 !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical: an early instance of the abstract 'Lefschetz element' viewpoint later central in combinatorial Hodge theory (Kähler packages, Adiprasito–Huh–Katz). It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lemma plus a toy counterexample in the abstract Lefschetz formalism of the standard conjectures. It is historically nice as an early 'Lefschetz element in an Artinian algebra' example, but elementary and slightly flawed (no Poincaré duality).
transcription_corrections: The relation list should read: L^4 = 0, L'^2 − LL' = 0, L^2 L' − L^3 = 0, L^3 L' = 0. This matches the transcription; the induced basis is 1 // L, L' // L^2, LL' // L^3 in degrees 0, 2, 4, 6. The 'deg: 0 2 4' under-labelling stops at 4, but L^3 is in degree 6.
The printed text visible beneath the ink is the Brauer III §8 typescript (it continues the previous page: 'à valeurs dans H^4(X, Z_ℓ[2]) ≃ Z_ℓ ...'). It is not part of the handwritten notes.
